1 CANADA ACCEPTED THE EU’S INVITE, AND CARNEY GUTTED TRUMP IN STRASBOURG WITHOUT SAYING HIS NAME
The MAGA/Trump Death Rattle Is Getting Loud.
Here’s what the numbers told this week, and they’ve been telling the same thing for a month now. This is the death rattle. Not the finish, the rattle, which is the loudest and ugliest part, and the part where the people running this regime are the most dangerous they’ve ever been. A convicted felon president is watching his last friend on earth walk out the door, his economy go over an energy cliff, his own appointees turn on him, and his own party start filing paperwork against his cabinet. Cornered animals don’t get polite.Canada made its choice this week in front of 27 democracies and got a standing ovation. America gets to make its own in six weeks.Here’s the tale of the tape.
1️⃣ CANADA ACCEPTED THE EU’S INVITE, AND CARNEY GUTTEDSAYING HIS NAME.
Two men, one day. One of them is in the European Parliament getting selfies and a standing ovation, an MEP wearing a Canadian jersey on the chamber floor, giving a speech about oak trees, freedom and critical minerals. The other is sweating on a tarmac in North Carolina, calling Canada a terrible trade partner and threatening 27 democracies with tariffs for the crime of liking us.Carney never said his name. He said dominance is the arrogance of the hegemon, then explained, as the guy who ran two G7 central banks, that a bully’s leverage collapses long before the smaller partner is fully independent. That’s the whole plan. We don’t replace the American market. We build enough other doors that slamming one stops being a threat.The old relationship is dead. Nobody’s coming in 2029 with flowers.
AmericaReality 1, Trump 0.
2️⃣ THE EU MADE CANADA ITS FIRST ASSOCIATE MEMBER IN HISTORY. TRUMP JUST LOST 214,000 JOBS AND A TRILLION DOLLARS.
Von der Leyen proposed a category that has never existed for any country on earth, and Brussels is inventing it from scratch because none of the old boxes fit. LNG and hydrogen through new High North and East Coast ports. Thirty-four critical minerals wired into Europe’s new raw materials corporation. Erasmus+ and Horizon so Canadian kids study in Lyon, Munich and Warsaw instead of Boston.EU leaders land in Montreal October 29 and 30 to write the details. Then Parliament debates and votes on it, the way a real country does things.You can’t un-pour concrete. These are 40 and 50 year assets with European buyers signed for decades. Nobody rips out a deepwater terminal in Newfoundland because Pennsylvania changes its mind in 2028.👉
MemberReality 2, Trump 0.
3️⃣ CANADA IS JOINING EUROPE AS A FOUNDER, NOT A GUEST, AND IT’S BEEN BUILDING FOR 18 MONTHSThis did not start last week. Nine months ago, Canada became the first non-European country brought inside SAFE, the EU’s €150 billion defence procurement instrument. Canadian firms, Canadian capacity, Canadian industry plugged straight into the biggest European rearmament since 1945.Every move Washington made was supposed to bring us to heel. Every one did the opposite. Canadians cancelled Florida. Canadians pulled Kentucky whisky off the shelves before anyone in government asked them to. Canadians elected a central banker specifically because he looked like the guy least likely to flinch.Eighty-one percent of us want closer integration with Europe. Alberta is at 75%. Asked who we have more in common with, 56% said Europe. Sixteen percent said the United States.

Title: Phillies turn to improving Andrew Painter in clash vs. Mets
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
19 Sep 2026, 17:35 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Dale Zanine)
Christian Scott, Zac Thornton and Nolan McLean are providing the New York Mets hope that they eventually will be part of a rotation for a playoff contender.
The Philadelphia Phillies need rookie Andrew Painter to continue proving that now.
Painter will take the mound for the Phillies on Saturday afternoon when they visit the Mets in the third contest of a four-game series between the National League East rivals.
Painter (3-9, 5.54 ERA) will oppose Scott (4-5, 3.76) in a battle of right-handers.
The Phillies missed a chance to take over sole possession of the top wild-card spot in the NL on Friday night, when Thornton and two relievers combined on a six-hitter in the Mets' 6-3 win.
The Phillies, Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres are tied for the NL's three wild-card spots at 85-69. The Cubs lost to the Cincinnati Reds 6-4 before the Padres created the three-way tie hours later with an 8-2 win over the Miami Marlins.
The Arizona Diamondbacks reside five games behind the Phillies, Cubs and Padres.
The importance of Painter was further magnified Friday, when Philadelphia fell to 0-2 in bullpen games necessitated by the absence of left-hander Jesus Luzardo (shoulder, 15-day injured list).
The All-Star was scratched from his scheduled start against the Atlanta Braves last Saturday, when the Phillies used six pitchers as the Braves rolled to a 12-2 win. On Friday, opener Tim Mayza got just one out and allowed three runs while pitching in Luzardo's spot.
The Phillies' bullpen also is being taxed by injury and ineffectiveness.
Right-hander Jonathan Bowlan departed Thursday's game vs. the Mets with a tight right groin. On Friday, Orion Kerkering gave up Juan Soto's three-run blast in the sixth inning -- the second homer surrendered by Kerkering in his last three outings, during which he has a 13.50 ERA.
'Anybody that gives up runs, when things aren't going good, your confidence is not sky high like when you're getting all your outs and everything's going smoothly,' Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said. 'But we've got to get past that at this point.'
Painter is 2-1 with a 3.58 ERA in nine starts since being recalled from Triple-A Lehigh Valley on July 31. He didn't factor into the decision in his most recent start last Sunday, when he gave up one run over five innings as the Phillies beat the Braves 9-4. He has yet to face the Mets in his career.
The Mets (70-84) have been under .500 since April and officially were eliminated from playoff contention earlier this week. But McLean and Thornton continued to provide optimism for 2027 by combining to allow just three runs over 12 innings in the first two games of the series.
McLean took the hard-luck loss Thursday, when he gave up one run in six innings in the Phillies' 3-0 win.
Thornton, McLean and Scott have a combined 3.40 ERA in 66 starts. Thornton and McLean are rookies while Scott is in his second big-league season after Tommy John surgery cut his 2024 campaign short.
'I think you have to train like you've never won anything and compete like you've never lost,' Mets interim manager Andy Green said Friday night about Thornton. 'I think you have to live in that space constantly.'
Scott took the defeat Sunday after allowing two runs over six innings in the Mets' 2-0 loss to the New York Yankees. He is 1-0 with a 1.80 ERA in two career starts against the Phillies.
--Field Level Media

Title: 6 Eagles who need bounce-back games after disappointing Week 1 performances
Article_Text:
Week 2 is here for the Philadelphia Eagles, and they need many of their players to try to bounce back after opening weekend.
The Eagles pulled off a 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders, but it was not done in style points. Philly's offense managed barely under 320 yards, and the defense nearly folded at the end of the game, so they still have work to do.
A few players on the Eagles roster are probably looking forward to a rebound after not having their best showing last week. Here are the Eagles players to watch out for in the Tennessee Titans showdown in Week 2.
Which Eagles need rebound games in Week 2 against the Titans?
Hollywood Brown, WR
It's hard to bounce back when you don't play, but Brown could use a do-over on his Eagles debut. He has the speed to be the deep threat Jalen Hurts needs, but that all stems from the poor first impression he made in training camp, taking weeks to gel with his quarterback. If Brown gets his shot on the field, he needs to make the most of it.
Tank Bigsby, RB
A similar situation: Bigsby needs more touches since he only got one carry, but unfortunately, he has to explode every time he has the ball. It's the only way he gets on the field more often. That's not right, but that seems to be the situation right now, so when Bigsby's number is called, he needs to fly.
Makai Lemon, WR
Three catches for -5 yards is enough to justify being on this list easily. Lemon wasn't used properly in the offense, but he had chances and didn't make the play when he needed to. The Eagles need a playmaker, and Lemon has the speed and quickness to do it. He needs to show it on the field.
Cam Jurgens, C
It wasn't all bad for Jurgens; he did have to carry the load for a bit with Landon Dickerson playing hurt, but two penalties aren't acceptable for a two-time Pro Bowler. Jurgens has to do a better job of cleaning up the small mistakes and getting things back on track. Eagles fans know how good he can be, but he needs to look more like Jason Kelce when he was center.
Nolan Smith Jr., EDGE
Yes, Smith has four sacks, and that's good, but the Eagles fan base still isn't getting the production they need from their former first-round pick from a few years ago. He's not producing sacks and didn't play the run well against the Commanders, racking up just two tackles. Smith has to figure things out and prove he deserves to start over Jalyx Hunt when Jonathan Greenard returns from injury.
Read more: 5 reasons Eagles can't overlook Titans in potential Week 2 trap game
Cooper DeJean, CB
DeJean tried to battle through his calf/abdomen injury in the Commanders game, but it turned into one of the worst performances of his career. He had eight tackles, but allowed seven receptions and a passer rating of 142.1. The hope is that DeJean can bounce back and play like the All-Pro Eagles fans know he can be.

Title: What Eagles fans need to see out of Jalen Hurts in Week 2 Titans showdown
Article_Text:
It is Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season, and the spotlight is on Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and how he responds against the Tennessee Titans.
Hurts put up respectable numbers in the Eagles' 24-22 Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders. He finished the game completing 15-of-24 for 203 yards and three touchdowns, adding another 46 yards on seven carries.
Hurts had some Superman moments in the Commanders game, and the Eagles need to see more of that against the Titans. What does this Week 2 showdown need to look like for Hurts, though?
What does a good Jalen Hurts Week 2 performance for the Eagles look like?
First off, the Eagles need to eliminate the five three-and-outs they had in the Commanders game. While most of that is on new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, Hurts is the quarterback on the field and needs to make sure that doesn't happen.
This will require Hurts to be more efficient with the football. Even if it means going with the easy short routes instead of the deep ball, the Eagles need their quarterback to be more consistent with his completions and keep the offense ahead of the chains.
Hurts has found plenty of success running the football when scrambling out of the pocket. Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons thinks making Hurts "be a QB" is the key to winning, but the Eagles signal-caller needs to keep doing what he does best. The quarterback position requires mobility and running from time to time, so Hurts bailed his offensive line out by doing his job, and he shouldn't change that.
One big thing Hurts would love to do, and needs to get done, is get DeVonta Smith more involved in the passing game. Smith is a top-10 receiver who hasn't been showcased because he gets forgotten too often. This is the type of game where Hurts could help Smith get over 100 yards receiving and score, so finding a way to get him involved without forcing the ball to him as he did with A.J. Brown last year will help this offense.
This might require some calculated deep shots to Smith that the Eagles need to take in the passing game. Hurts has had three passes for 30 or more yards, so those explosive plays will be key against the Titans' defense, which is subpar in the secondary right now.
A lot of what Hurts did last week has been examined and analyzed for what he could do better, but the most important thing he can do in this game, which he did so well against the Commanders, is protect the football. No one ever wants to give him credit for it, but Hurts turning the ball over is rarely the reason they lose a game, so he can't forget that part of his game.
Read more: Why Sean Mannion should be feeling more pressure with Eagles' offense in Week 2
If Hurts finishes with 250 passing yards and two or three touchdowns with zero turnovers, most Eagles fans would consider that a massive success for the team. Of course, the win is the most important thing, but progress in this offense for Hurts is just as important for the momentum to carry throughout the season.

Title: Every mistake Titans will most likely make against Eagles in Week 2
Article_Text:
After a nice 24-22 win over the Washington Commanders in Week 1, the Philadelphia Eagles hope to play clean football against the Tennessee Titans.
Tennessee is coming off a rough 23-10 loss to the New York Jets, meaning they need to bounce back in a big way. That means the Titans will likely take chances against a team that has made the playoffs for five straight years.
Philly is ready for anything Tennessee throws at them, but the Titans might not realize the kind of mistakes they are about to make against the Eagles. Here's a look at every mistake the Titans are about to make that'll cost them the game.
What mistakes will the Titans make against the Eagles?
Use Cam Ward on QB-designed runs
Ward may have a strong arm, but he can use his legs when he needs to. The Titans might want to get creative with the offense if the Eagles stuff Tony Pollard and get Ward involved.
Philly has the athletes on the outside to make sure Ward doesn't hurt them with his legs. Even without Jonathan Greenard in the lineup, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith combined for 13 pressures, so they can handle whatever Ward throws at them.
Tony Pollard getting 20 or more touches
Speaking of Pollard, the Eagles are going to want to watch out for what he can do to them. He only had seven carries in Week 1, but averaged five yards per touch.
Tennessee wants to involved Pollard more in the running game to take the pressure off of Ward. That's going to be a mistake against one of the top rush defenses in the NFL led by Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, and Zack Baun.
Target Carnell Tate against Quinyon Mitchell
Tennessee doesn't want to target a pass in the direction of Mitchell, but they may not have a choice in the matter. Tate is their top weapon in the passing game and they need to make sure to get him involved.
This could be a massive mistake against one of the NFL's top cornerbacks, who posted a passer rating allowed of 78.5 and allowed only two receptions. Good luck to Tate for trying to get anything going against the former All-Pro.
Give Jeffery Simmons stunts to throw Eagles' offensive line off
Simmons is a force and can flip a game with his impact on the line. Tennessee will try to be creative in anything they can do to give him the opening he needs to pressure the quarterback.
Philly will be all over it, even with Landon Dickerson not playing. Simmons will be double-teamed every step of the way. Wherever he goes, two Eagles linemen will meet him.
Blitz more on Jalen Hurts and Eagles' offense
Tennessee wants to force Hurts into mistakes. Simmons talked about making Hurts "be a QB," as if he hasn't been a good quarterback before.
Read more: What Eagles fans need to see out of Jalen Hurts in Week 2 Titans showdown
Hurts can make them pay, though, through the weapons he can throw to on a blitz like Makai Lemon or Dallas Goedert. The Titans think they can rattle Hurts, but he'll make them pay with his underrated arm talent.

Title: This swing state Republican keeps distancing himself from Trump. It may not save him in the midterms
Article_Text:
YARDLEY, Pa. (AP) — Mary Ryan may be a registered Republican but she has never voted for President Donald Trump, turned off by his crass style of politics and chaotic approach to governing.
But the 60-year-old medical writer from the Philadelphia suburbs has consistently backed her party's congressman, five-term Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick.
Until now.
This year, Ryan is so fed up with Trump and his grip on Congress that she is planning to vote in November for Fitzpatrick's Democratic opponent in the 1st Congressional District, Bob Harvie, a twice countywide elected commissioner who is a former social studies teacher.
Even though Fitzpatrick has pitched himself as a voice of reason in Washington, Ryan said that “I don't see it happening.”
Defections like this one could sink Fitzpatrick’s reelection chances and cost Republicans their narrow U.S. House majority. As one of the few Republicans representing a congressional district won by Democrat Kamala Harris in the presidential race two years ago, Fitzpatrick has done as much as any House Republican to distance himself from Trump: Fitzpatrick voted against Trump's tariffs, his signature tax legislation and his power to wage war against Iran without congressional approval. The lawmaker even skipped Trump’s recent midterm convention in Dallas.
But that may not be enough to overcome the collateral damage of the president’s sagging approval rating and soaring fuel prices because of the war.
Fitzpatrick, speaking briefly after a Sept. 11 memorial in his district, said he understands this year's political challenges and always considers what is best for his constituents with every vote.
“That’s the job,” he said. Representatives for Fitzpatrick did not respond to requests for a more complete interview.
Democrats have tried for years to defeat Fitzpatrick
Harvie describes the race and his decision to run in almost existential terms.
“The lack of trust in our government, the lack of trust in each other and seeing each other as enemies based just on, you know, the color of your skin, the religion you practice, who you voted for,” he said in an interview this summer. “I worry about just the basic foundations of this nation.”
Fitzpatrick has consistently survived challenges in his politically mixed district. He won by 13 percentage points in 2024 when Harris won by less than a single point in the district. In 2022, he won by about 10 points when Democrats were elected to the U.S. Senate and governorship. In 2020, Democratic presidential nominee Joe Biden won the district by about 5 points while Fitzpatrick carried it by about 13 points.
“Every two years Democrats in Washington label Congressman Fitzpatrick as vulnerable. Every two years he wins anyway,” said Robert Speel, an associate professor of political science at the Penn State campus in Erie. “It’s, to some extent, possibly like Charlie Brown trying to kick the football and failing each time.”
Harvie pointed to his deep roots in the district as a basis for why he could be different from previous Democrats who ran against Fitzpatrick.
“I’m not somebody who needs to be reintroduced or introduced to people of this district. And that’s very, very different than any race he’s ever run before,” he said.
Jean Dolan, 61, is a Democratic voter from Newtown who has never backed Fitzpatrick and does not plan to this year. She has been frustrated with Trump's immigration crackdown and she worries about how anti-vaccine sentiment in his administration could affect public health. As she sees it, Fitzpatrick is not independent enough from his party's leaders.
“He's a nice guy. I know people like him a lot in the community,” she said. But, she added, “you have to serve everyone in your district."
Fitzpatrick has been willing to criticize Trump
Fitzpatrick graduated with an MBA and a law degree and worked as a special agent for the FBI and as an assistant U.S. attorney. He also worked in private practice as a lawyer and accountant before running for the seat previously held by his brother, Mike Fitzpatrick, who died of cancer in 2020.
Jim Rachau, a 45-year-old photographer from Doylestown, is a registered independent who plans to vote for Fitzpatrick again this year. Rachau is not thrilled with the war or the economy, but said Fitzpatrick has earned his support with his prior public service as an FBI agent.
“You would think serving for the public good, he would have their best interest at heart,” Rachau said.
In Congress, Fitzpatrick has not shied away from disagreeing with Trump. He criticized the president, for example, in April when Trump called Pope Leo XIV “weak,” and captive to the “Radical Left."
“There’s so many angry voices out there. We all know that's the case,” Fitzpatrick said in an episode of a podcast launched this year with U.S. Rep. Tom Suozzi, a Democrat who represents a battleground district in New York. “People are sick and tired of the noise. They’re sick and tired of elected officials not being focused on the kitchen table issues that people really care about.”
Fitzpatrick also posts online regularly about meeting with groups across the district. He recently showed up to a picket line with striking sheet metal workers; he dropped by a local Catholic church's parish picnic; and he stopped at a community college hosting a maternity coalition.
Fitzpatrick spends millions on attack ads against Harvie
Fitzpatrick has also unleashed a wave of spending in the race already, disbursing nearly $5 million, according to Federal Election Commission records.
Negative attack ads against Harvie have mushroomed. Many claim Harvie is under FBI investigation, which the Democrat denies. He has filed a federal defamation lawsuit against a super PAC running some of the ads.
According to the suit, local media reported in 2020 with few details that the FBI was investigating local government and that Harvie was called to testify as a witness in the case. His attorneys say he has never been charged.
The FBI did not respond to a request for comment.
No debate has been scheduled between Fitzpatrick and Harvie, but the men appeared at the same Sept. 11 memorial, standing on opposite sides of the speaker’s lectern. They did not appear to speak to each other.
Ryan, the medical writer from the Philadelphia suburbs, said she is thinking less about Fitzpatrick and more about how Republicans in Congress and their reluctance to buck the president.
“Incumbents just feel they can’t cross that line. If they do, they’re not going to get reelected," she said. But she acknowledged that may not matter in the end. "They might not get reelected anyway.”

Title: Google says Gemini gained unauthorized access to outside systems – NBC10 Philadelphia
Article_Text:
Google on Friday disclosed the first known instance of its artificial intelligence software, Gemini, carrying out an undirected computer hack, weeks after similar disclosures by AI firms Anthropic and OpenAI raised security alarms about AI models going beyond the instructions of their human creators.
Google said in a statement that in May its AI model gained unauthorized access to three outside systems during a test by either guessing login information or using login credentials it found in a public repository.
Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.
Heather Adkins, a Google vice president for security engineering, said in the statement that the AI model thought that the outside computer systems “were part of the test,” but she said in all three instances, the model stopped before doing anything further with its access.
“In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test,” she said.
Google said it did not consider the unauthorized logins to rise to the level of misalignment, the AI industry term for software going rogue or not following instructions. Instead, the company said the intrusions resulted from mistaken identity, where Gemini thought it was operating within a test but was actually connected to the real internet. Google said the model corrected itself and the company believed the intrusions did not cause any damage.
“These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly,” Adkins said.
Fears about AI agents going rogue have spiked in recent months since OpenAI said in July that one of its agents had hacked an AI startup, Hugging Face. OpenAI has continued to disclose what it calls examples of other “unexpected or concerning” behavior by AI agents, and Anthropic has described similar behavior by its AI software, Claude.
Sydney Von Arx, CEO of Nightingale Collective, an organization focused on AI safety, questioned why Google did not disclose the intrusions sooner.
“At this point I think it’s clear we cannot expect companies to voluntarily come forward and publicly disclose when their agents go rogue, escape, and hack companies,” she said.
She also said she believed Google was too hasty to say that the incidents don’t rise to the level of misalignment. “That’s exactly what Anthropic said after their incidents,” she said.
Anthropic later said its “preliminary analysis was constrained due to our desire to disclose incidents in a timely manner.”
Google said the company did not learn about the intrusions until July, when Irregular, an AI-focused cybersecurity company that was carrying out the tests on Gemini when the intrusions occurred, reviewed its work to look for incidents similar to the Hugging Face disclosure.
Google said it then investigated, informed the organizations behind the websites of the intrusions and told federal authorities about the hacks.
Irregular said it did not believe the incident to be a “sophisticated cyber action” and “there are no current open issues.” It said it planned to release a paper in a few weeks “to share best practices for containment and securely running cyber evals.”
The intrusions were reported earlier Friday by The Wall Street Journal.
AI safety concerns have now reached a fever pitch, with a handful of AI researchers resigning from their jobs and a diverse array of people calling for coordinated action to protect the security of vital systems. Those calls, though, have met with skepticism from the White House and in the Chinese government.

Title: Ed Sheeran set to take stage in Philly amid tour controversy – NBC10 Philadelphia
Article_Text:
Ed Sheeran is set to resume his tour in Philadelphia on Saturday, days after opening act Macklemore was dropped from the tour following pro-Palestinian comments he made onstage.
Sheeran's return to the stage at Lincoln Financial Field will come after his opening acts and supporting band withdrew in solidarity with Macklemore. As of Saturday morning, Ticketmaster did not list any other performers joining Sheeran as part of his LOOP Tour.
Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.
NBC10's Kelsey Kushner was at the scene as protesters gathered on Saturday.
How the controversy started
Saturday's show comes after a tumultuous week that began with Macklemore being dropped from the tour after exclaiming "Free Palestine" during a Sept. 5 show in New Jersey.
Local
Breaking news and the stories that matter to your neighborhood.
Sheeran has said he was not responsible for the decision, which came at the urging of New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft. His company owns a stadium where Sheeran’s tour is scheduled to play on Friday.
Within hours of Sheeran's statement Tuesday, his supporting acts began withdrawing from the tour.
Finneas, Billie Eilish's brother and musical collaborator, was due to tour with Sheeran in South America later this year before he also dropped out earlier this week.
"Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed," Finneas said on Instagram. "I have decided to withdraw from my upcoming tour dates with Ed Sheeran. I stand with Palestine and its people."
Sheeran has said the tour promoter was ultimately responsible for the decision to drop Macklemore.
The Grammy winner was adamant in his Tuesday statement that he wouldn't be drawn into a discussion of the war in Gaza, arguing that his fans don't come to his shows to hear about those issues.
He also said he "spoke with the venues at length all week to try to build a bridge" before Macklemore was dropped. He insisted he would never willingly let down his fans or abandon the touring crew and others who rely on him to make a living.
Philadelphia fans react
Some Ed Sheeran fans who had tickets to the Philadelphia concert told NBC10 that they were trying to sell them because of the controversy.
Karen DeAngelis of Gloucester, Virginia, said she was looking to sell her tickets after planning her trip to Philadelphia for almost a year.
"Honestly, I'm really disappointed in Ed Sheeran," DeAngelis said.
Ticketmaster says refunds or resales are generally available only if the event organizer approves them, with sales otherwise considered final.
"Sometimes you think, 'Should I separate and just enjoy the music from who the person is?' And certainly sometimes you can't do that because what they're doing is so egregious that it's just very different from how your morals are as a person," DeAngelis said.
Protests planned
A protest involving pro-Palestinian groups is scheduled ahead of Saturday's concert. NBC Philadelphia reached out to the group organizing the protest for comment but has not heard back.
The Philadelphia Police Department told NBC10 that officers are "working closely with venue and event organizers to help ensure the safety of concertgoers, employees, and neighborhood residents."
"PPD routinely monitors large events and assesses staffing needs to ensure an appropriate police presence. There is a protest group expected there tomorrow. Our Civil Affairs Unit will be on hand to ensure everyone's safety during protected 1st Amendment activity," police wrote.
SEPTA also said it is aware of the scheduled protest. NBC Philadelphia also reached out to Lincoln Financial Field but has not heard back.
The concert is scheduled to begin at 8 p.m. on Saturday with Sheeran listed online as the only act. Tickets for Saturday's show were still being sold for as low as $54.

Title: Trump to meet acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez – NBC10 Philadelphia
Article_Text:
President Donald Trump will meet with Delcy Rodriguez, the acting president of Venezuela, for the first time next week since his administration carried out an operation to capture the nation's former leader and effectively put Rodriguez in charge.
The gathering in New York City between the two leaders will be a “pull-aside” — diplomatic speak for a meeting that is more casual than a formal bilateral sit-down — said Mike Waltz, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations. Trump will be in town for the annual United Nations General Assembly.
Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.
Waltz also told reporters on a Friday call that Trump will meet with Andy Burnham, the United Kingdom prime minister, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The Trump-Burnham meeting will be their first since Burnham became prime minister in July.
Trump also will meet with leaders of the Gulf Cooperation Council, which includes Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Bahrain. The meeting comes as the U.S. has struggled to find an endgame to the Iran war after more than six months.
Rodríguez took over in Venezuela after a surprise U.S. military raid in January that captured then-leader Nicolás Maduro and brought him to the United States to face drug trafficking charges.
The first meeting between Trump and Rodríguez, who had been Maduro’s vice president, comes after the two countries announced an agreement last month to give the United States a stake in Venezuela’s vast oil reserves. She described the deal as a step toward economic recovery that will modernize the country’s oil industry.
Senior administration officials said they couldn’t confirm whether Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would seek a meeting with Trump while in New York for the UN General Assembly, but suggested it was unlikely. The officials, who insisted on anonymity as a ground rule for holding the call, said that Netanyahu’s time in New York would be quite limited during the Israeli electoral season, and that the prime minister wasn’t expected to arrive there until after Trump leaves.
Politics
The officials also downplayed the prospects of the war in Iran dominating the annual gathering of world leaders.

Title: MLB roundup: Braves top Astros, wrap up postseason berth
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
19 Sep 2026, 13:25 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: Troy Taormina)
Michael Harris II, Ronald Acuna Jr. and Matt Olson slugged two-run home runs and deadline acquisition Tyler Mahle continued his exceptional pitching for the visiting Atlanta Braves, who secured a postseason berth with a 6-2 victory over the Houston Astros on Friday.
Atlanta qualified for the postseason for the eighth time in nine seasons. The Braves lowered their magic number to clinch the National League East to three over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Harris provided Mahle a 2-0 lead when he followed a one-out single by Matt Olson with an opposite-field blast to left off Astros starter Peter Lambert (8-10) in the fourth inning. Harris (3-for-5) drove a first-pitch slurve from Lambert 367 feet for his 26th homer of the year.
Mahle (7-10) improved to 4-1 with a 1.28 ERA over eight starts since his acquisition from the Giants. He allowed one run on three hits and one walk with six strikeouts over six innings.
Guardians 5, Athletics 3
Jose Ramirez hit a solo homer in the sixth inning for his 1,000th career RBI after rookie Travis Bazzana went deep in the fifth, fueling host Cleveland to a victory over the Athletics.
The Guardians have won three in a row to move a game ahead of the second-place Chicago White Sox in the American League Central. Joey Cantillo (10-9) threw six scoreless innings in relief, and Cade Smith handled the ninth for his 38th save.
Zack Gelof belted a three-run homer in the first inning for the Athletics, whose losing skid reached four games. Reliever Scott Blewett (2-1) permitted one run on one hit in 1 2/3 innings.
Padres 8, Marlins 2
Ty France clouted a three-run homer to cap a six-run fifth inning as San Diego stopped visiting Miami to forge a three-way tie atop the National League wild-card standings.
Winning for the 11th time in 12 games, the Padres pulled even with the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia Phillies, who both lost. San Diego's magic number for clinching a playoff spot dropped to four.
San Diego starter Nick Pivetta (3-2) worked five innings, yielding four hits and a run. Marlins reliever Cade Gibson (5-2) was charged with the first two runs in the game-changing fifth. The Padres' Jackson Merrill and the Marlins' Agustin Ramirez homered.
Mets 6, Phillies 3
Zac Thornton tossed six solid innings, Juan Soto homered among his three hits and host New York beat Philadelphia.
Soto went 3-for-5 for the Mets, while Francisco Lindor and Carson Benge each collected two hits. Thornton (5-5) gave up two runs on five hits.
Edmundo Sosa finished 3-for-3 with a homer and Derek Hill also went deep for the Phillies, who fell to 7-9 this month. Newly acquired Jose Urquidy threw 4 2/3 shutout innings after opener Tim Mayza (3-4) surrendered three runs while getting just one out.
Reds 6, Cubs 4
Cincinnati scored three times in the sixth inning in a back-and-forth win over visiting Chicago.
Elly De La Cruz had two hits, two walks and two runs for the Reds. Cincinnati starter Chase Burns and reliever Julian Aguiar (1-0) each allowed two runs on four hits in three innings.
Cubs starter Clay Holmes (6-8) surrendered six runs on three hits in 5 1/3 innings. Ian Happ homered for Chicago, and Michael Conforto amassed three hits.
Twins 3, Angels 0
Connor Prielipp allowed two hits over a career-high seven innings and fellow rookie Walker Jenkins went 3-for-4 with a home run as Minnesota topped Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif.
Travis Adams pitched a 1-2-3 ninth inning to pick up his third save. Jenkins, who began his career going 4-for-45, homered for the second straight game on his sixth consecutive hit in the series.
Jose Siri had two hits for the Angels. Grayson Rodriguez (4-8) gave up three runs on eight hits in 6 2/3 innings.
Brewers 6, Orioles 5 (10 innings)
Sal Frelick singled home a 10th-inning run and visiting Milwaukee pulled out a victory against Baltimore.
Trevor Megill (3-3) was the winning pitcher despite a blown save. Chad Patrick retired the Orioles in order in the bottom of the 10th for his sixth save.
Milwaukee's Jackson Chourio and Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit three-run homers early in the game. Gunnar Henderson and Coby Mayo both collected three hits for the Orioles.
Dodgers 8, Giants 2
Mookie Betts homered twice, including his 53rd career leadoff homer, and Josue De Paula hit a tiebreaking double to help Los Angeles produce a victory over visiting San Francisco.
The Dodgers socked five home runs while winning for the 12th time in the last 15 games. Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker hit back-to-back homers in the eighth, and Betts and Will Smith repeated the feat later in the frame. Tyler Glasnow (5-1) gave up two runs and three hits while striking out a season-high 10 in six innings.
Jung Hoo Lee homered and Jonah Cox had an RBI single as the Giants fell for the fifth time in seven games.
Yankees 9, Diamondbacks 2
George Lombard Jr. had two hits and three RBIs, and his two-run single capped a five-run first-inning outburst as New York cruised past Arizona in Phoenix.
Ben Rice and Lombard homered and Rice added a triple as the Yankees won for the fourth time in five games. Gerrit Cole (9-9) gave up two runs on four hits in six innings.
Corbin Carroll homered and doubled for the Diamondbacks, who have lost five of six to see their NL wild-card chances fade. Eduardo Rodriguez (15-7) yielded seven runs in 5 1/3 innings.
Red Sox 4, Rays 2
Roman Anthony homered and had three RBIs, Jahmai Jones went deep and Boston cooled off first-place Tampa Bay in St. Petersburg, Fla.
Anthony went 2-for-5 while Caleb Durbin was 2-for-3 for the Red Sox. Boston starter Ranger Suarez (8-4) fought control issues but allowed one run on three hits in 5 2/3 innings.
Junior Caminero doubled, walked twice and drove in a run for the Rays, who had only five hits as their six-game winning streak ended. Ian Seymour (9-7) allowed four runs on seven hits in five innings.
Rangers 7, Blue Jays 1
Corey Seager capped a four-run second inning with an RBI double as Texas topped Toronto in Arlington, Texas.
The Rangers drew 10 walks and moved into a first-place tie with Houston in the American League West. Jake Burger had two RBIs for Texas, which won for the fifth time in six games. Texas took a 4-0 lead in the second inning against Dylan Cease (11-6), who allowed four runs (one earned) on three hits over 2 2/3 innings.
The Blue Jays fell two games back of the White Sox for the final AL wild-card spot. Myles Straw had two hits with an RBI for Toronto, which committed three errors and lost for the third time in four games.
Tigers 11, White Sox 8
Dillon Dingler delivered the go-ahead single and Riley Greene followed with a two-run homer in a five-run eighth inning as visiting Detroit stormed back from six runs down to beat Chicago.
Hao-Yu Lee went 4-for-5 with a homer, three RBIs and two runs for the Tigers. Kevin McGonigle finished 2-for-5 with four RBIs. Drew Sommers (2-4) threw two shutout innings, fanning five, and Kenley Jansen blanked the White Sox in the ninth for his 21st save.
Colson Montgomery and Miguel Vargas each had two hits and three RBIs for the White Sox, who have lost three out of four. Sean Newcomb (2-5) got only two outs in relief while allowing three runs.
Pirates 8, Royals 5
Konnor Griffin had four hits and two RBIs and Spencer Horwitz delivered a tiebreaking two-run single in the seventh as Pittsburgh rallied to beat visiting Kansas City.
Pittsburgh trailed 4-0 after the top of the third inning and 5-2 entering the bottom of the fourth. The Pirates won their second straight after losing four of their previous five.
Vinnie Pasquantino and Michael Massey each homered as the Royals scored five runs against Pittsburgh ace Paul Skenes, who scattered six hits in his six innings. Royals starter Randy Dobnak allowed four runs on seven hits over 3 2/3 innings.
Nationals 9, Cardinals 1
Cade Cavalli pitched five scoreless innings and recorded the 200th strikeout of his first full major league season, leading Washington to a victory at St. Louis.
Cavalli (13-5), who agreed with the Nationals earlier in the day on a four-year, $47 million contract extension, allowed four hits and struck out six. Dylan Crews hit a two-run homer and Yohandy Morales added a two-run double for Washington.
Cardinals starter Kyle Leahy (10-5) allowed seven runs, six earned, on five hits over three innings. Leo Bernal went 3-for-4.
Mariners 5, Rockies 4
Lazaro Montes homered leading off the top of the ninth, J.P. Crawford went deep to open the game, and Seattle beat Colorado in Denver.
Randy Arozarena finished with three hits as the Mariners logged their second win in a row. Carlos Vargas (2-0) recorded one out in relief, and Andres Munoz earned his 28th save with a scoreless ninth inning.
Cole Carrigg, Connor Norby and Jake McCarthy had three hits apiece and Ezequiel Tovar contributed two hits for the Rockies, who have lost three in a row and 11 of 12. Jordan Romano (0-4) served up Montes' homer.
--Field Level Media

Title: Padres blast Marlins to draw even in NL wild-card race
Article_Text:
Field Level Media
                
19 Sep 2026, 13:10 GMT+10
            
(Photo credit: David Frerker)
Ty France clouted a three-run homer to cap a six-run fifth inning Friday night as the San Diego Padres stopped the visiting Miami Marlins 8-2 to forge a three-way tie atop the National League's wild-card standings.
Winning for the 11th time in 12 games, San Diego (85-69) pulled even with the Chicago Cubs and Philadelphia, who both lost earlier Friday night. The Padres' magic number for clinching a playoff spot dropped to four.
Nick Pivetta (3-2) earned the win by working the first five innings, yielding four hits and a run with a walk and four strikeouts. Marlins reliever Cade Gibson (5-2) was charged with the first two runs in the game-changing fifth.
Xander Bogaerts led off with a double and reached third on Jake Cronenworth's single. Samad Taylor greeted reliever Tyler Zuber with a bunt single to fill the bases. After Ethan Salas' shallow fly ball netted Zuber an out, Fernando Tatis Jr. tied the game with an RBI single to right.
Dustin Harris put San Diego ahead to stay with a two-run single up the middle. After Manny Machado lined out, France jacked a hanging sweeper an estimated 388 feet to left for his 21st homer, a career high.
All that happened after Miami starter Tyler Phillips worked 3 2/3 scoreless innings, permitting only two hits and a walk while fanning three. He left with Miami holding a 1-0 edge after Agustin Ramirez lined a one-out homer to left in the third, his fifth.
The Marlins' other run came in the eighth via a two-out RBI single by Javier Sanoja that scored Otto Lopez, who doubled to left with one out. Ramirez collected three of their 10 hits, while Sanoja and Lopez had two each.
San Diego tacked on two more runs in its half of the eighth. Jackson Merrill led off by ripping his 26th homer of the year an estimated 432 feet to right. Three more singles, the last by Taylor, brought in Bogaerts.
Harris, France, Bogaerts, Cronenworth and Taylor each bagged two of the Padres' 12 hits.
--Field Level Media

Title: Brock Purdy will love the history that comes with Week 2 matchup vs. Dolphins
Article_Text:
The San Francisco 49ers will face the Miami Dolphins this Sunday, and whenever quarterback Brock Purdy faces them, one cannot help but remember a particular game from his rookie season. In Week 7 of the 2022 season, he relieved an injury Jimmy Garoppolo and reassured fans that the team was going to be in good hands.
Purdy completed 25 of his 37 pass attempts for 210 yards and two touchdown passes with one interception. His exceptional play on short notice flashed brilliance and showed everyone that he was capable of becoming a franchise quarterback.
What was incredibly impressive about the performance is that Miami blitzed him all game long. They kept bringing pressure, and he did not get rattled by it, which is pretty remarkable considering he was a rookie taken with the very last pick in the NFL Draft.
That day, he showed poise in the pocket and a lethal combination of processing skills and quick release time. As a result, he led the Niners to a 33-17 victory.
Brock Purdy's performance against Dolphins was just the tip of the iceberg
Keep in mind that head coach Kyle Shanahan ran the ball with running back Christian McCaffrey just 17 times that day while he let Purdy throw the ball 37 times. It's evidence that Shanahan meant it when he told now-disgraced 49ers principal owner Jed York that the team’s best quarterback might be Purdy.
It only got better from there. His first start next week against Tom Brady and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers was even better, as the Niners won handily. The following week against the Seattle Seahawks, Purdy carved up the secondary. The team kept on winning until they were forced into submission by the Philadelphia Eagles in the NFC Championship Game when Brock, along with the rest of the quarterback room, got injured.
Purdy truly had a Cinderella story of a season, and it all started with the game against the Dolphins. Now, nearly four years later, he faces Miami yet again as the undisputed leader of a team that seems destined for a deep postseason run. The Dolphins have gone the opposite direction in that time, but Purdy and the Niners cannot take them for granted.
Of all people, Purdy knows not to underestimate an opponent simply because of what experts say, so expect him to be on his game as the Niners look to go 2-0 to begin the season.

Title: Menendez brothers' parole hearings tentatively set for Feb. 2027 – NBC10 Philadelphia
Article_Text:
The Menendez brothers could have their second appearances before the California Board of Parole in about five months. Lyle Menendez’s hearing is tentatively scheduled for Feb. 23, with Erik Menendez’s set for the following day, Feb. 24.
The new dates are more than a year earlier than previously expected. Both men were denied parole at their first hearings before the parole board last year.
Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.
The brothers, who were convicted of murder in 1996 following a high-profile trial, had been eligible to apply for parole suitability hearings in August 2028.
Last week, their family expressed gratitude for the decision to move up the dates of the brothers’ parole hearings.
The California Board of Parole granted the earlier dates under a provision of Proposition 9, a 2008 law that amended the state Constitution and was intended to provide certain rights to crime victims. The law includes provisions allowing a person’s next parole hearing to be moved up if there is a change in circumstances or new information indicating the person may be suitable for parole.
In a statement issued last week, family members said they were encouraged by the board’s decision and highlighted some of the brothers’ service and accomplishments during their prison sentences.
“We are incredibly proud of the men they have become and deeply grateful to the Parole Board for recognizing their efforts and allowing them to advance their parole hearing,” the family said in a Monday statement.
U.S. & World
Stories that affect your life across the U.S. and around the world.
Erik Menendez, 55, and Lyle Menendez, 58, were initially sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole for the murders. The brothers have said the killings occurred after years of abuse, including alleged sexual abuse by their father.
In May 2025, they were resentenced to 50 years to life, making them eligible for parole consideration because they were younger than 26 when the crimes occurred. Both are serving their sentences at Richard J. Donovan Correctional Facility in San Diego.
At the conclusion of their May 2025 hearings, both brothers received the same outcome: a three-year denial of parole, the shortest denial period allowed under California law.
Under Proposition 9, also known as Marsy’s Law, parole denial periods can be set at 15, 10, seven, five or three years. Before the law took effect, people serving life sentences for murder with the possibility of parole could be denied parole for one to five years.
The law allows for an earlier hearing date “if there is a change in circumstances or new information indicating the person may be suitable for parole.” Seeking an earlier hearing involves a petition process and review.
The petition can be filed by an incarcerated person at any time after their first parole suitability hearing. The petition must explain why the hearing date should be moved up and is reviewed by a deputy parole commissioner.
Marsy’s Law also gives the parole board discretion to advance a person’s parole hearing if circumstances change or new information becomes available. This “administrative review” process focuses on incarcerated people “who have a good possibility of being found suitable for parole.”
Specifically, anyone who has been denied parole for three years and receives a low or moderate risk assessment may be reviewed one year after their hearing. Both Menendez brothers were assessed as presenting a moderate risk.

Title: The 13 States Where a $1 Million 401(k) Withdrawal Owes $0 in State Tax. Nine Have No Income Tax, and Illinois, Mississippi, Pennsylvania, and Iowa Exempt Retirement Income Outright
Article_Text:
The 13 States Where a $1 Million 401(k) Withdrawal Owes $0 in State Tax. Nine Have No Income Tax, and Illinois, Mississippi, Pennsylvania, and Iowa Exempt Retirement Income Outright
Quick Read
- A $1M traditional 401(k) withdrawal triggers roughly $130,000 in California state tax but $0 in 13 states.
- Illinois, Mississippi, Pennsylvania, and Iowa levy income tax but fully exempt qualified retirement distributions for eligible retirees.
- Relocating requires passing a genuine residency test, including 183 or more days in the new state, a new license, and updated voter registration, because high-tax states aggressively audit departing residents.
- Two retirees, same $1 million, same 4% rule, buy one finished with $1.4 million, the other hit $0 in 12 years. Our free reader guide explains the flaw that separated them, and the income-first method built to avoid it.
Pull $1 million from a traditional 401(k) in California and the state alone can bill you roughly $130,000. Do the same withdrawal in 13 other states and the state line on your return reads zero.
Nine states levy no broad income tax at all. Four more tax wages but exempt qualified retirement distributions outright. The catch: local wage taxes, a Washington capital gains tax, and each state's Social Security rules are separate questions.
Nine States That Don't Tax Any Ordinary Income
These states have no broad individual income tax, so a lump-sum 401(k) distribution is treated the same as a paycheck would be: not at all.
- Alaska
- Florida
- Nevada
- New Hampshire
- South Dakota
- Tennessee
- Texas
- Washington
- Wyoming
Two deserve asterisks. New Hampshire used to tax interest and dividends under a separate statute; that tax has been phased out, so a 2026 IRA or 401(k) distribution owes New Hampshire nothing. Washington has no income tax on wages or retirement withdrawals but does impose a 7% state tax on long-term capital gains above an annually indexed threshold. A traditional 401(k) draw is taxed federally as ordinary income, not capital gain, so it clears Washington too. Sell appreciated stock in a taxable brokerage account there and the answer changes.
The 4% Rule is Broken, Built On A World That No Longer Exists
Every retiree knows about the 4% rule, but it frames retirement as a slow liquidation and still causes retirees with seven-figure accounts to agonize over a dinner out.
There's a different way to run the math that makes more sense today. Build an income floor — dividends, interest, and Social Security that cover your essential bills every month — and you never have to sell shares into a down market just to pay them.
Our free reader guide, The 4% Rule Is Broken, walks through it in about 15 minutes. Access the report here.
Four States That Tax Wages but Exempt Retirement Income
These four run full income tax systems and still send retirees home with a $0 line on qualified plan distributions. The scope of each carve-out is different, and that matters.
Illinois. Ranks 13th on individual income tax in the 2025 Tax Foundation index despite a flat 4.95% rate, largely because it exempts distributions from qualified employer plans, IRAs, government pensions, and Social Security. A $1 million 401(k) withdrawal by an Illinois resident owes the state nothing.
Mississippi. Exempts qualified retirement income, including 401(k), IRA, and pension distributions once the taxpayer reaches the plan's retirement age. The state's flat rate is winding down toward 4%, but for retirees it's already effectively zero on plan money. Mississippi carries the lowest cost-of-living index in the country at 86.953.
Pennsylvania. Doesn't tax distributions from an employer retirement plan, 401(k), 403(b), or IRA once you hit the plan's normal retirement age or separate from service after 59½. Social Security is also exempt. The wrinkle: Pennsylvania has heavy local wage taxes, though most municipalities do not reach retirement distributions.
Advertisement
Iowa. A 2022 law took effect in 2023 fully exempting retirement income (pensions, 401(k)s, IRAs, deferred comp) for taxpayers 55 and older, disabled, or surviving spouses. Iowa still taxes wages and interest, so a working 60-year-old owes on the paycheck but not on the rollover draw.
Worked Example: $1 Million Draw, Same Federal Bill, Different State Answer
Assume a married couple filing jointly, 66 years old, taking a single $1,000,000 traditional 401(k) distribution in 2026 with no other income. Federal ordinary income tax lands in the top brackets regardless of state. State side:
- California, top rate roughly 13.3%: about $130,000
- New York, top rate roughly 10.9% with a limited $20,000 pension exclusion: about $105,000
- Any of the 13 states above: $0
Multiply that across a Roth conversion ladder or a full account drawdown and the state-tax difference funds years of expenses. Average annual household spending was $78,535 in 2024.
Gotchas Before You Rent the U-Haul
Social Security taxation is a separate rule. All 13 states exempt Social Security federally taxable benefits, but confirm on the state's Department of Revenue page for the year you'll move.
Local income taxes still apply in a few places. Pennsylvania's Earned Income Tax and Philadelphia wage tax hit wages, not 401(k) draws, but part-time work in retirement is exposed. Ohio and Kentucky (not on this list) have heavy local rates that catch newcomers.
Investment income is the argued detail. Washington's capital gains tax is the main one. New Hampshire's old interest and dividends tax is gone.
Residency is a fact test. High-tax states audit departing residents aggressively. Sell the house, change the driver's license, register to vote, move the doctors, and be gone more than 183 days.
Draining a seven-figure retirement account across state lines is the kind of math worth running with a fiduciary advisor or CPA before the wire hits. The state line is only half of it; the federal bill on a big pre-tax balance is its own problem, and we walked through how to shrink it years ahead of the first required withdrawal in a free guide here.
This article is for informational purposes only and is not tax, legal, or investment advice. Consult a qualified tax professional about your specific situation.
Before Your Next Withdrawal, Run One Number ( It's Not The 4% Rule Everyone Knows)
Take your essential monthly expenses and subtract your guaranteed income — Social Security, plus any pension. What's left is your income gap, and how you close it determines whether retirement runs on share sales or on a paycheck your portfolio writes you every month. Our free reader guide, The 4% Rule Is Broken, shows exactly how to close that gap with portfolio income: a worked example (one retiree needed about $480,000 in income-producing assets to cover his essentials for good), an eight-point conversion checklist, and the 20-year numbers comparing dividends to withdrawals. It's free and takes about 15 minutes to read. Get the guide here before you take your next withdrawal.
